title: Webhook Echo
content:
**Echo** is Gravito's enterprise-grade webhook handling system. It provides secure receiving with signature verification and reliable sending with automatic retries, supporting multiple providers like Stripe, GitHub, and custom HMAC sources.

The Webhook Engine

Echo orchestrates your entire webhook lifecycle, ensuring secure ingestion and reliable dispatch without the boilerplate of manual HMAC verification or retry logic.

SECURE_INGEST

Built-in HMAC-SHA256 signature verification and timestamp tolerance checks to prevent replay attacks.

RELIABLE_SEND

Exponential backoff retry strategy with configurable multipliers and maximum delay for outgoing webhooks.

EVENT_DRIVEN

First-class Orbit module for PlanetCore. Register semantic event handlers for specific provider actions.

Installation

bun add @gravito/echo

Receiving Webhooks

Using OrbitEcho

Install Echo as an Orbit in your PlanetCore application to leverage container-based verification.

import { PlanetCore } from '@gravito/core'
import { OrbitEcho } from '@gravito/echo'

const core = new PlanetCore()

// Install Echo with provider configuration
core.install(new OrbitEcho({
  providers: {
    stripe: {
      name: 'stripe',
      secret: process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
      tolerance: 300 // timestamp tolerance in seconds
    },
    github: {
      name: 'github',
      secret: process.env.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET!
    }
  }
}))

// Get receiver and register event handlers
const receiver = core.container.make('echo.receiver')

// Handle specific events
receiver.on('stripe', 'payment_intent.succeeded', async (event) => {
  console.log('Payment received:', event.payload)
  // Process payment...
})

receiver.on('github', 'push', async (event) => {
  console.log('Push event:', event.payload)
  // Trigger deployment...
})

Webhook Endpoint Architecture

Create a unified route to handle incoming webhooks from multiple providers.

app.post('/webhooks/:provider', async (c) => {
  const provider = c.req.param('provider')
  const body = await c.req.text()
  const headers = Object.fromEntries(c.req.raw.headers)
  
  const receiver = c.get('echo.receiver')
  const result = await receiver.handle(provider, body, headers)
  
  if (!result.valid) {
    return c.json({ error: result.error }, 401)
  }
  
  return c.json({ received: true })
})

Manual Verification Strategy

For standalone implementations or custom handlers, verify signatures manually using the low-level API.

import { WebhookReceiver } from '@gravito/echo'

const receiver = new WebhookReceiver()
receiver.registerProvider('stripe', process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!)

app.post('/webhooks/stripe', async (c) => {
  const body = await c.req.text()
  const headers = Object.fromEntries(c.req.raw.headers)
  
  // Verify signature
  const result = await receiver.verify('stripe', body, headers)
  
  if (!result.valid) {
    return c.json({ error: 'Invalid Signature' }, 400)
  }
  
  // Process event type-safe
  if (result.eventType === 'payment_intent.succeeded') {
    // Handle payment
  }
  
  return c.json({ received: true })
})

Sending Webhooks (Reliable Dispatch)

Dispatch webhooks to external services with built-in retry mechanisms and exponential backoff.

import { WebhookDispatcher } from '@gravito/echo'

// Create dispatcher with retry configuration
const dispatcher = new WebhookDispatcher({
  secret: process.env.OUTGOING_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  retry: {
    maxAttempts: 5,
    initialDelay: 1000,      // 1 second
    backoffMultiplier: 2,    // Double delay each retry
    maxDelay: 300000,        // 5 minutes max
    retryableStatuses: [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
  },
  timeout: 30000  // 30 seconds
})

// Dispatch webhook
const result = await dispatcher.dispatch({
  url: 'https://example.com/webhook',
  event: 'order.created',
  data: { orderId: 123, total: 99.99 },
  id: 'webhook-123' // Optional: custom webhook ID
})

if (result.success) {
  console.log('Webhook delivered:', result.statusCode)
} else {
  console.error('Delivery failed:', result.error)
}

Supported Ecosystem

Echo includes native logic for major industry providers, ensuring zero-config verification for common platforms.

ProviderSignature MethodVerification Header
stripeHMAC-SHA256 + TimestampStripe-Signature
githubHMAC-SHA256X-Hub-Signature-256
shopifyHMAC-SHA256X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256
slackHMAC-SHA256 + TimestampX-Slack-Signature
genericHMAC-SHA256X-Webhook-Signature

Custom Provider Implementation

Implement the WebhookProvider interface to support bespoke signature protocols while leveraging Echo's handling logic.

import { WebhookProvider, WebhookReceiver } from '@gravito/echo'

class MyProvider implements WebhookProvider {
  readonly name = 'my-provider'

  async verify(payload: string, headers: Record, secret: string) {
    // Custom verification logic
    const signature = headers['X-Custom-Signature']
    const expected = computeHmacSha256(payload, secret)
    
    return {
      valid: signature === expected,
      payload: JSON.parse(payload)
    }
  }
}

// Register custom provider type
const receiver = new WebhookReceiver()
receiver.registerProviderType('my-provider', MyProvider)
receiver.registerProvider('custom', 'secret', { type: 'my-provider' })

Event Handlers & Logic

Register semantic handlers for specific provider events or catch-all listeners for auditing.

const receiver = c.get('echo.receiver')

// Handle specific event type
receiver.on('stripe', 'payment_intent.succeeded', async (event) => {
  // Atomic payment processing
})

// Handle all events from a provider (Global Auditor)
receiver.on('stripe', '*', async (event) => {
  console.log('Stripe audit:', event.eventType, event.payload)
})

// PROTOCOL_ADVISORY: SECURITY_POSTURE

Echo automatically validates HMAC signatures and verifies timestamps to prevent replay attacks. In production, always enforce HTTPS and rotate your secrets quarterly.

Architecture: Best Practices

✓ IDEMPOTENCY

Use a unique delivery ID to ensure handlers can process the same event twice without side effects.

✓ ASYNC_QUEUE

For heavy operations, acknowledge the webhook immediately and offload processing to a queue.

✓ LOG_AUDITING

Maintain a log of all incoming payloads for debugging and historical conflict resolution.

✓ TIMEOUT_MANAGEMENT

Enforce strict timeouts on outgoing webhooks to prevent stalling the internal dispatch pipeline.

**Architect's Insight:** Webhooks are the
of distributed systems. Echo brings order to this chaos by providing a standardized, secure, and resilient infrastructure. It's the silent bridge between your application and the external world.
